Hi Asha — thanks for the clear brief and the ramp sketch. This is exactly the kind of planning that avoids spikes during launches. I looped Karthik (infra) and Marissa (AM) to help put together an operational sketch + commercial framework.

High level answers to your bullets:
- Staged ramp (24–36 months): we can model stepped commits with quarterly true-ups. Each step can include a capped overage rate and an annual recalibration where you can move steps earlier if adoption accelerates.
- Triggered burst: we offer a scheduled-burst add-on where you reserve a burst window ahead of a launch (recommended lead time: 72 hours for predictability). For unscheduled urgent bursts we can enable a short-notice pool but price and capacity guarantees differ.
- Auto-opt-in: we can do an auto-renew with an annual true-up clause (preferred for customers who want less admin). We can also add an opt-out window before renewal.

Next steps from our side:
1) Karthik will provide a short doc that maps how the burst behavior looks from a runtime perspective and what the expected latency/cost profiles are.
2) Marissa will propose a commercial sketch (two variants: 24-month phased ramp and 36-month phased ramp) with indicative discounts/credits for longer commitments and for locking burst buckets in advance.
3) I'll assemble everything into a single one-pager and share.

Hi Asha — quick operational sketch attached below (inline summary). Happy to walk through live.

Summary: 
- Regular staged commit: each commit step provisions dedicated pool capacity with autoscale headroom. Sequence length assumptions and concurrency targets most impact how committed capacity maps to latency.
- Scheduled bursts: when you book a scheduled burst window (recommended >=72h notice) we pre-warm KV cache and reserve a transient capacity pool; response latency should remain within your current SLOs. Billing: bursts are invoiced as dedicated burst-hours at a premium rate but they do not consume committed units while active.
- Short-notice bursts: possible via global residual pool; faster to enable but no latency SLA and higher per-hour charges.

Operational constraints / lead time: 
- Pre-warm time: ~30–60 minutes for common models if KV cache primed; full warm requires the 72h window for heavy models.
- Maximum single-burst scale: depends on region capacity and reserved nodes; we can commit a burst ceiling in the contract.

I'll include a small matrix mapping typical latency/pricing buckets based on concurrency. If you want, we can template two scheduled-burst bookings for your upcoming product release windows.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Asha — following up on Kimberly and Karthik's notes with two commercial sketches attached: 24-month phased ramp (Option A) and 36-month phased ramp (Option B). Key differences:

Option A — 24 months
- Step schedule: quarterly increases (4 steps, front-loaded second year)
- Burst credit: 4 scheduled burst windows included per year (each up to 48 hours)
- Discount: 8% on committed units year-over-year; annual true-up allowed

Option B — 36 months
- Step schedule: semi-annual increases (6 steps)
- Burst credit: 6 scheduled burst windows included per year
- Discount: 12% applied and an onboarding credit in year 1

Other notes: co-terming multiple products into a single agreement is supported. We recommend a single umbrella agreement with product-specific appendices so runs and quotas are explicit per product. For auto-renew: we propose an opt-out window of 60 days prior to renewal and an annual true-up that consolidates usage across the umbrella.

If this looks directionally correct, I'll produce a near-term amendment draft that includes: the step schedule, the burst ceiling, pricing ladder, and the true-up mechanism. Can we target the week of Aug 16 to review the amendment?
